Questions, answered.

The things project managers and installers ask us most. Anything else, just email the project.

How do I get a quote?

Email your project to projects@americangraphiccontractors.com the way you already have it: drawings or mockups, photos, a site list or a quick note. AGC AiSSIST reads it first and checks it against our 99 Questions, then a project manager comes back to you with what is clear, what is still missing and anything that affects price, such as access, removals or after-hours work. Once those points are answered, you get a quote for the scope as confirmed. For a repeat program, tell us which past job it matches and we start from that scope.

What should I send with a request?

Whatever you already have is a good start. The details that make a quote accurate are: site addresses and an on-site contact; graphic sizes and quantities, or the mockups and drawings that show them; the material and laminate if the graphics are already printed; the surfaces they go on; whether anything old has to come off first; and your target dates and preferred work window. If a detail is missing, we ask before we quote, not on install day.

Do you print the graphics?

No. AGC is an installation partner, not a printer. You or your print partner produce the graphics and ship them to the site or to our crew; we receive them, install them to your specifications and document every location. Because we are not selling print, our advice on materials, sizes and site conditions is about what installs well, and we are glad to work alongside your existing print producer.

Can you quote day and after-hours work?

Yes. On request we price a daytime window (8 am to 5 pm) and an after-hours window (5 pm to 11 pm) side by side, so you can choose per location. After hours often suits busy downtown sites, malls and stores that can’t have crews on the floor while they’re open; daytime is usually simplest where the space is closed or your own. Weekend work can be scheduled too.

Do you offer site surveys?

Yes. Before anything is printed or quoted, we can visit each location to measure every surface, photograph it and note its condition: paint, texture, existing films or graphics, obstructions and access. You get the measurements and photos to build artwork from, so files are sized right the first time. For programs, surveys can be scheduled across many locations at once, and a survey isn’t always needed if you already have accurate drawings.

What are the 99 Questions?

They are the questions our project managers ask before every quote, gathered into one checklist: scope, site conditions, surfaces, materials, access, permits, timing and close-out. We use them to catch the details that cause delays and surprise costs later. They are available as a free eBook, so your own team, from sales and design to project management, can use the same checklist when briefing any install.

Get the free eBook ↗
Where do you install?

Across the United States and Canada. AGC has rated installers in 21 U.S. states and 9 Canadian provinces and has installed at more than 950 locations, from a single storefront to programs spanning hundreds of sites. Crews are matched to each job by location and skill, so the work is done locally to one AGC standard.

Can you work after hours?

Yes. We schedule around your business so stores, branches and offices keep running: daytime, after hours, overnight or weekends. Tell us your opening hours and any quiet periods when you send the project, and we plan the work window, crew size and visit order around them. Where a site has its own rules, such as mall access times or venue check-in, they go into the schedule before the crew is booked.

Do you remove old graphics?

Yes. Removals are part of everyday work for our crews: expired campaign vinyl, old signage and letters, window film, wall graphics and retail fixtures. Crews clear adhesive residue and can patch and paint old fastener holes, so the surface is clean and ready for the next install. If old graphics need to come down before new ones go up, include it in the request so it is quoted and scheduled as one visit.

What about permits, lifts and access?

We confirm site logistics before a crew is booked: the on-site contact, check-in or badge rules, loading and parking, and any permits, for example when work near a street might need a closure. For work at height we confirm lift needs and safe tie-off points. If the site has rules of its own, like mall access windows or venue badges, they go into the job details so the crew arrives prepared.

Does the surface matter?

A lot. Freshly painted walls need time to cure before vinyl bonds properly, textured or uneven surfaces need the right material and technique, and existing window films change how new film sits on the glass. That is why we ask what the surface is, and when walls were last painted, before install day. If a surface isn’t ready, we would rather tell you before the crew arrives than after.

What safety gear do your crews use?

Crews wear PPE suited to the job, and it is standard AGC policy whenever we work with rigid signage. For work at height we confirm lifts and tie-off points in advance. If your site has its own safety rules or induction, tell us when you book and the crew will follow them.

Can you run a national rollout?

Yes. One AGC point of contact plans the whole program with you, from the first site survey to the final close-out. Every request is checked against our 99 Questions, crews are matched to each location by area, skill set and project type, and every detail is confirmed before work starts. Each site is installed to your brand standards and closed out with end-of-day reports and photos, so a program of hundreds of stores is handled the same way as one.

What do I get after the install?

End-of-day reports with photos for every location, so you can see what was installed and how it looks without visiting. Programs also get close-out documentation for each site, all tracked in Client Flow, where you can check status, photos and files at any time. Installers record any issues, such as damaged graphics, in their close-out notes, so nothing gets missed.

What is Client Flow?

Client Flow is your project portal. For every location it shows status and scope, files, the install schedule, a map of your sites, shipping and tracking, pricing and approvals, install photos and the weather around the install date. Updates appear as work happens, so your team and AGC always look at the same information. You can try the interactive preview in the AGC Flow section.

What is AGC AiSSIST?

AGC AiSSIST is our own AI, working behind every project. It reads incoming requests, checks them against our 99 Questions to flag anything missing, and makes sure every email, PO and photo lands on the right project. People stay in charge: our project managers review and approve what it does. It also powers the free tools on this site, like the Project Scope Checker.

How do I get into my portal?

Tap My Portal at the top of the page and enter the email address AGC has on file for you; that email is what connects you to your client or installer portal. If you are new or your email has changed, use Request access in the same window, or call 1 (877) 395-7435 and we will set you up.

How do I pay an invoice?

Online, through Make a Payment: the cart button in the header takes you straight to the payment page. For questions about an invoice, email projects@americangraphiccontractors.com or call 1 (877) 395-7435.

Make a Payment ↗
How do installers work with AGC?

Email projects@americangraphiccontractors.com with your company name, the cities and regions you cover, the types of work you do (for example window film, wall graphics, signage or fixtures) and equipment such as lifts. Jobs you are assigned come with files, scope, schedule and site details in Field Flow, and you close each job out there with photos and notes.

What is Field Flow?

Field Flow is the installer app. Each job has its files, scope, schedule, a map, shipping and tracking, the local weather forecast and a close-out step in one place. Installers submit close-out photos and notes about what was completed and any issues, which feed straight into the client’s reports. You can try the interactive preview in the AGC Flow section.

What does AGC-rated mean?

It is an installer who has completed work for AGC and been rated on it. Along with location and skill set, ratings help us match the right crew to each job. More than 580 installers carry an AGC rating today.

Do you offer training?

Yes, in several ways. AGC University on YouTube has free install videos. On this site, the AI Install Tutor answers install questions and runs quick quizzes, and the Installer Tool Finder suggests tools for a job. The free 99 Questions eBook covers project intake from the first brief.

Watch AGC University ↗
Which tools do your crews recommend?

The Installer Tool Finder on this site lists the tools our crews recommend: squeegees and buffers, knives and cutters, heat guns, ladders and platforms, wrap tools, removal tools, safety gear and cleaning supplies. Search or browse by category, or describe the job and it builds a kit for you. Product links go to Amazon.

One site or one hundred. Let’s get it done right.

No forms. Email your project the way you already have it: drawings, photos, a site list or a quick note. AGC AiSSIST picks it up from there and gets it to your project lead with what’s clear and what’s still needed.
